div.head: VI Atr 40.1
div.ab: Forðam þurh þæt hit sceal on earde godian to ahte, þæt man unriht alecge ⁊ rihtwisnesse lufige for Gode ⁊ for worlde.
Forþam þurh þæt hit sceal on earde godian to ahte, þe man unriht alecge ⁊ rihtwisnesse lufige for Gode ⁊ for worlde.
For it is only by the suppression of injustice and the love of righteousness in matters both religious and secular that any improvement shall be obtained in the condition of the country.
Denn um etwas [Bedeutendes] wird es im Lande besser werden dadurch, dass man Unrecht beseitige und Gerechtigkeit pflege in Geistlichem und Weltlichem.
For things will become considerably better in the land through putting down injustice and loving righteousness in matters spiritual and secular.
div.note: Here the law perhaps ends (according to the paraphrase and II Cn 11.1); what follows (the ‘Appendix’, 41–49) also appears separately in homiletic collections (so-called Wulfstan, ed. Napier pp. 307, 179). Liebermann compares V Atr 33.1.
